incidents.victim: US, Ukrainian and allied officials, military, journalists and political figures
incidents.vector: Phishing messages impersonating commercial messaging app (e.g. Signal) support accounts to trick high-value targets into surrendering verification codes, account PINs and backup recovery keys.
incidents.impact: FBI and CISA updated their warning that Russian intelligence actors have taken over individual messaging accounts to read private and group message history; a stolen backup recovery key can compromise even a re-created account on the same number.

incidents.victim: John Bolton (former US National Security Advisor)
incidents.vector: Compromise of Bolton's personal email account, which he had used to send classified 'diary' notes to unauthorized family members after leaving office in 2019.
incidents.impact: Disclosed via Bolton's guilty plea to mishandling national defense information; an Iran-linked actor accessed the account containing TOP SECRET/SCI material, including foreign military plans and intelligence from human sources.

incidents.vector: Breach of KDDI's public email service infrastructure, also used by five other Japanese internet service providers.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole the data of more than 14 million users of the shared email service in an incident earlier in the month.

incidents.vector: USB drives infected with Chinese malware were connected to classified military networks.
incidents.impact: A potential leak of classified data went undisclosed for nearly a year until uncovered by reporters; Japanese officials are notifying NATO partners of the possible exposure.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack of undisclosed method against Ukrposhta's digital services.
incidents.impact: The attack took down Ukrposhta's mobile app and several web services; the operator is working to restore service.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asian government bodies and state-owned energy infrastructure
incidents.vector: ASPX web shells deployed via vulnerable web applications, followed by SoftEther VPN, Mimikatz, JuicyPotato and a new custom .NET backdoor (TinyRCT) for command execution and data theft.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 tracked cluster CL-STA-1062 compromising at least ten Southeast Asian organizations, including two state-owned critical energy entities, exfiltrating databases and web-server source code.

incidents.victim: Turla espionage targets — Ukrainian government/military and Italian foreign-policy entities
incidents.vector: Multi-component .NET backdoor (STOCKSTAY) disguised as a stock-market tool, using encrypted WebSocket C2 for file theft, screen capture and command execution.
incidents.impact: Google attributes STOCKSTAY to Russia's FSB-linked Turla group, deployed since at least December 2022 for ongoing cyber-espionage against Ukrainian and Italian-foreign-policy targets.

incidents.victim: Hospitality and hotel organizations in Europe and Asia
incidents.vector: Phishing emails laundered through Calendly and Google redirect infrastructure deliver photo-themed ZIP archives containing fake-image LNK files that launch obfuscated PowerShell and a Node.js implant.
incidents.impact: Microsoft tracked an active campaign since April 2026 targeting hotel front-desk staff, establishing persistent access via dual registry persistence and C2 beaconing; ultimate objective unclear but appears to be staging for follow-on activity.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a third-party vendor that allowed attackers to load malicious code onto Polymarket's website.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole roughly $3 million before the breach was detected; Polymarket will reimburse affected users.

incidents.vector: 2022 credential-stuffing attack reusing leaked username/password pairs to take over accounts, then adding attacker-controlled payment methods.
incidents.impact: Third and final defendant ('Snoopy') sentenced to 18 months; the 2022 attack compromised ~60,000 accounts and stole about $600,000, with access to other accounts resold on criminal markets.

incidents.vector: Rogue SD-WAN peering and stolen certificates to access Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, then exploitation of zero-day CVE-2026-20245 via a malicious CSV upload to create a root 'troot' account.
incidents.impact: Mandiant found an attacker gained root-level control of the provider's SD-WAN orchestrator — enabling broad visibility into internal traffic — and used extensive anti-forensic cleanup; full scope could not be determined.

incidents.vector: Breach of a contractor that managed the agency's mobile device management platform, linked to a wave of attacks on Ivanti EPMM servers.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole names, phone numbers and email addresses of Belgian intelligence service employees.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack affecting Bajaj Auto and its technology subsidiary, Bajaj Auto Technology Limited.
incidents.impact: One of India's largest vehicle manufacturers disclosed the incident to regulators and took containment measures; threat actor, data theft and any ransom demand were not disclosed.

incidents.victim: Global victims of Amadey loader and StealC infostealer (140,000+ computers)
incidents.vector: Amadey loader used for initial access then StealC infostealer to harvest credentials, cookies and session tokens; sold as malware-as-a-service feeding access brokers and ransomware crews.
incidents.impact: Microsoft DCU, Europol and partners disrupted the operations — 326 servers, 142 domains and $47M in crypto seized; the tools had infected 140,000+ computers and stolen 27M+ credentials over their lifetime.

incidents.vector: Mass scanning and brute-forcing escalated to exploiting unpatched FortiGate CVEs and a custom 'FortigateSniffer' that intercepted credentials across 24 protocols; hashes cracked on a GPU cluster and validated inside victim networks.
incidents.impact: The 'FortiBleed' campaign exposed valid admin and SSL VPN credentials for ~73,932 firewalls across 194 countries, including a Turkish NATO defense contractor; network access is being sold on, and infrastructure remains active.

incidents.victim: Transport for London; SSM Health and Sutter Health (US)
incidents.vector: Social-engineering and SIM-swapping intrusions by the Scattered Spider group; the August 2024 Transport for London attack disrupted its systems.
incidents.impact: Two members pleaded guilty in the UK; one also admitted hacking US healthcare providers. The wider group is tied to 120 intrusions, 47 US victims and at least $115M in ransom payments.

incidents.vector: Intrusion claimed by the World Leaks extortion group, which listed the company on its leak site.
incidents.impact: World Leaks claims to have stolen more than 200,000 documents, allegedly including sensitive data on Apple and Tesla electronic components; Tata confirmed a security breach.

incidents.victim: Klue customers — LastPass, Snyk and other firms
incidents.vector: Compromise of a legacy integration credential at business-intelligence platform Klue, then theft of customers' OAuth tokens used to pull data from their connected Salesforce accounts.
incidents.impact: At least eight companies, including several security firms, had Salesforce data stolen; a group calling itself Icarus is extorting Klue and threatening to leak the data.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion of undisclosed method.
incidents.impact: The university is rebuilding its entire IT infrastructure following a hack the prior week.

incidents.vector: Initial access via the Trivy supply-chain compromise (attributed to TeamPCP), then misuse of a secret Amazon API key to access the Commission's Europa.eu AWS environment.
incidents.impact: CERT-EU attributes a March 19 breach in which ~92GB of data — names, email addresses and some content affecting 42 internal clients and 29+ EU entities — was stolen and later appeared on ShinyHunters' leak site.

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem — LiteLLM, Red Hat packages, Mercor and others
incidents.vector: Compromised maintainer/GitHub accounts used to publish poisoned packages laced with credential-stealing Shai-Hulud worm variants (e.g. 'Miasma'); LiteLLM PyPI packages and 32 Red Hat packages were trojanized.
incidents.impact: Malicious LiteLLM versions (~3M daily downloads) could expose cloud credentials, API keys and crypto wallets across tens of thousands of environments including Mercor; Red Hat pulled 32 affected packages (~117K weekly downloads).

incidents.vector: Takeover of the 'ehindero' npm maintainer account to publish 140+ poisoned Mastra packages depending on a malicious dayjs typosquat ('easy-day-js'), whose postinstall hook ran an obfuscated dropper and fetched a second-stage Node.js implant.
incidents.impact: Microsoft attributes the compromise to North Korea's Sapphire Sleet; any workstation or CI/CD pipeline running npm install/update of the poisoned versions risked theft of credentials, tokens and build environments.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of FortiSandbox flaws CVE-2026-39808 (OS command injection) and CVE-2026-39813 (path traversal), bypassing authentication and escalating privileges for arbitrary command execution.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed dozens of exploitation events from multiple operators on commodity infrastructure; compromise of these trusted security appliances could grant elevated access in sensitive environments.

incidents.victim: US and Canadian medical, academic and military research institutions
incidents.vector: Exploitation of externally facing REDCap research servers and deployment of custom INFINITERED malware to harvest credentials, then abuse of domain content-compliance rules to silently BCC-forward emails for exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Google's UNC6508 remained undetected for over a year (since September 2023) pursuing AI, defense, cyber and medical research; known victims are assessed to be only a fraction of a larger, ongoing campaign.

incidents.victim: Council of Europe, universities and other ShinyHunters victims
incidents.vector: Data theft and extortion, including exploitation of an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft flaw to breach universities; stolen data posted to a Tor leak site.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters added the Council of Europe to its leak site, threatening to release 297GB of allegedly stolen data, and is actively extorting universities exploited via the Oracle vulnerability.

incidents.victim: Major Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Tejarat, Saderat, EDBI)
incidents.vector: Attack against communications infrastructure shared by the four banks.
incidents.impact: Online portals and mobile apps for four of Iran's largest banks were down over a weekend; intelligence sources believe Israeli hackers were likely responsible. The banking council said no customer data was accessed.
